extraction.summary: A 68-year-old female was admitted on 03/11/2026 with right lower lobe Streptococcus pneumoniae pneumonia and secondary sepsis, presenting with productive cough, rigors, dyspnea, and new acute confusion. She was managed in the high dependency unit with IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, fluid resuscitation, and oxygen support, successfully transitioning to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. By discharge on 09/11/2026, her mental status and oxygenation fully normalized on room air, and inflammatory markers improved significantly (CRP decreased from 288 to 41 mg/L). She is discharged home to complete 2 remaining days of oral antibiotics with outpatient primary care and specialist follow-up.
extraction.clinical_reasoning: The patient exhibits significant clinical improvement and stabilization following treatment for S. pneumoniae bacteremic pneumonia and sepsis. Reassuring findings include full resolution of acute encephalopathy/confusion, normal vital signs on room air (SpO2 96%, RR 18, HR 88, Temp 37.4 C), normalization of leukocytosis (WBC 9.8 x10^9/L), and dramatic reduction in inflammatory marker CRP (from 288 to 41 mg/L). Areas requiring ongoing post-discharge monitoring include residual elevated CRP (41 mg/L), mild renal impairment (creatinine 94 umol/L), sub-optimal glycemic control (HbA1c 7.8%), mild anemia (Hb 11.9 g/dL), and clarification of penicillin allergy status after uneventful beta-lactam therapy during admission.
recommended_next_steps: Complete remaining 2 days of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily.
Schedule GP review within 7 days for repeat CRP and renal function panel.
Schedule diabetes nurse review regarding glycemic management for HbA1c of 7.8%.
Obtain repeat chest radiograph in 6 weeks to confirm radiological resolution of right lower lobe consolidation.
Refer to allergy clinic to formally assess and potentially de-label penicillin allergy.
missing_critical_info: Baseline renal function (creatinine) to differentiate mild chronic kidney disease from resolving acute kidney injury.
